program_items.summary: ARN NEGATIVE__CAPABILITY_ABSENT attributed to extraction (sparse) and abstraction (none) stages. Mapping failed (worse than band control 0.489 vs 0.506). Typed licence and abstention mechanisms absent.

extraction.mechanism: Stopword-filtered content tokens (top 12 by frequency) as roles; within-sentence co-occurrence (window<=4) as relations
extraction.deficit: Flat bag-of-words style extraction misses semantic structure, negation scope, and role hierarchy. No dependency parsing, no entity recognition, no relation typing.

abstraction.mechanism: No abstraction stage - reducer outputs flat SupportStructure with atoms+edges
abstraction.deficit: No hierarchical abstraction levels, no intermediate concepts, no causal/process abstraction. Structure is purely surface lexical co-occurrence.

mapping.result: Worse than band control (0.489 vs 0.506 confirmatory exact)
mapping.deficit: Simple coverage ratio insufficient for structural analogy. No role typing, no relation semantics, no partial mapping credit, no cross-level mapping.

typed_licence.mechanism: No applicability mechanism, no boundary/QoI statement, no preserved/non-preserved relation classification
typed_licence.deficit: ARN reducer cannot express applicability conditions, scope restrictions, or boundary/QoI. Cannot abstain on insufficient evidence (CANNOT_CHECK only if <2 roles or 0 relations)

abstention.mechanism: CANNOT_CHECK only when insufficient extraction evidence (<2 roles or 0 relations)
abstention.result: CANNOT_CHECK rate 0.0 on confirmatory (no abstention despite poor performance)
abstention.deficit: No principled abstention on uncertain mappings, missing decisive evidence, or scope violations. System is forced to ACCEPT/REJECT even when analogy is unclear.

program_items.root_cause_summary: ARN reducer is a deterministic surface lexical matching system with no deep semantic extraction, no abstraction hierarchy, and no applicability reasoning. The negative confirms that shallow bag-of-features extraction is insufficient for scientific analogy decisions.
